text:
Alex Kim: Heads-up — Large customer wants "auto-spillover" from Dedicated -> Hosted when their pool fills. They want it on by default. What do we need on the telemetry/console side before we let this escape the pilot?
Priya Desai: Need to decide what signals we surface to the customer. If we show "spillover_count" live in their dashboard, ops teams can deduce capacity and routing behavior. Risky.
Diego Morales: Agreed. Also need to cap tokens and force a cheaper model variant on spillover. Otherwise cost/quality explodes.
Nora SRE: From an isolation POV we must ensure tenant A's spillover never impacts tenant B's latency SLOs in hosted pools. That means separate queues + throttles.
Jen Park: UX side: customers expect to see "failover occurred" events. We can expose a high-level event but not raw capacity numbers. Maybe: "fallback_event: true" + reason enum.
Sam Product: We should also expose which model variant we fell back to (e.g., quantized variant) and an estimate of quality delta. Transparency matters.
Alex Kim: OK proposals floating: 
  1) Emergency-only spillover toggle (off by default).
  2) Per-spillover token cap + forced model_variant.
  3) Aggregate fallback events in console (no raw capacity metrics).
  4) Telemetry labeled as "sanitized" for customer-facing dashboards.
Diego Morales: Implementation sketch (routing policy snippet):
```yaml
routing_policy:
  on_dedicated_exhaust:
    enabled: true
    mode: "emergency_only" # admin toggle
    spillover_target: hosted
    spillover_model_variant: "redwood-small-q4_0"
    token_cap_per_minute: 5000
    expose_metric_to_customer: "sanitized_fallback_count" # aggregated boolean/percent, no raw capacity
```
Priya Desai: Concerning telemetry leak: even an aggregated percent over short windows can be gamed. Recommend smoothing to 1h windows and floor values at >1% resolution.
Nora SRE: Also add internal-only metrics: per-hosted-pool-utilization and per-tenant-spillover_tokens for debugging. These must be behind admin RBAC.
Jen Park: Console UX: show a "Fallbacks" timeline entry with: timestamp, fallback_model (small-q4_0), token_consumed (rounded), and "reason" enum (DEDICATED_EXHAUST). No raw pool IDs or host names.
Sam Product: For SLAs we need to document that spillover is best-effort and quality may differ. Also allow customers to opt-out entirely.
Diego Morales: Edge-case: if hosted capacity absolutely unavailable we should fail closed (return 429 or explicit fallback flag) rather than silently queue forever.
Alex Kim: Security + privacy: do not expose anything that reveals our hosted capacity across regions. That was a big ask from legal — no per-region capacity chart.
Priya Desai: Telemetry naming conventions: prefix internal metrics with "internal." and customer-facing metrics with "public.sanitized." Add retention rules.
ops-bot: deploy-check: routing-policy-service:ok, telemetry-aggregator:ok
Nora SRE: One more ops note: implement a circuit-breaker that trips if spillover rate > X% of hosted pool for Y minutes, and then block further spillover to protect the hosted customers. + alerting to infra on-call.
Jen Park: Quick mock for console copy: "Your Dedicated pool temporarily used hosted fallback. Model downgraded to reduce cost. See rollout settings to change behavior." Keep it simple.
Diego Morales: Action items: @Jen to update console mocks + copy (ETA: Thu), @Diego to land routing_policy changes + unit tests (ETA: Fri), @Priya to write telemetry naming & aggregation doc (ETA: Tue next week), @Nora to define SRE circuit-breaker thresholds (ETA: Mon).
Sam Product: I'll update the customer contract language for Dedicated spillover and add opt-out checkbox in provisioning flow.
Alex Kim: Thanks all. If there's no blocker we'll ship the emergency-only option behind a flag and run a small pilot with customer-provided guardrails.
Priya Desai: P.S. Let's add a short eval: does quality regression on small-q4_0 vs main model exceed our "noticeable" threshold for that customer workload. If yes, we must refuse auto-spillover and only allow manual escalation.
Alex Kim: Noted — add to the pilot checklist.
